/-!
# The flux identity with a source

The inhomogeneous clock equation `∂ₜ²u = Δu + Vu + f` has the same energy computation as the
homogeneous one, with one extra term: the source pairs with the time derivative. Everything else
cancels exactly as before, so

`∫ ∂ₜ(energy density) = 2∫ ((V+1)·u·∂ₜu + f·∂ₜu)`.

The extra pairing is what a Picard iteration on the Duhamel formula controls, so this identity is
the entry point to an existence proof by the energy method.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open MeasureTheory

open scoped ContDiff

section Source

variable {d : ℕ} {u V f : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ) → ℝ} {K : Set (Fin d → ℝ)} {t : ℝ}

/-- The clock equation with a source. -/
def SolvesWaveEqSource (u V f : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ), waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u) p
    = (∑ i : Fin d, waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u) p)
      + V p * u p + f p

/-- A source-free solution is the special case of a vanishing source. -/
theorem solvesWaveEqSource_zero (h : SolvesWaveEq u V) :
    SolvesWaveEqSource u V (fun _ => 0) := by
  intro p
  rw [show ((fun _ : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ) => (0 : ℝ)) p) = 0 from rfl, add_zero]
  exact h p

/-- **A source is absorbed into the potential wherever the field does not vanish**, so the
inhomogeneous equation is the homogeneous one for a modified potential off the zero set. -/
theorem solvesWaveEq_of_solvesWaveEqSource (h : SolvesWaveEqSource u V f)
    {p : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ)} (hp : u p ≠ 0) :
    waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u) p
      = (∑ i : Fin d, waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u) p)
        + (V p + f p / u p) * u p := by
  rw [h p]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **The pointwise energy identity with a source.** -/
theorem waveDirDeriv_energyDensity_source (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u)
    (hsolve : SolvesWaveEqSource u V f) (p : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ)) :
    waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (energyDensity u) p
      = 2 * (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u p
          * ((∑ i : Fin d, waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i)
              (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u) p) + V p * u p + f p))
        + (∑ i : Fin d, 2 * (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u p
            * waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u) p))
        + 2 * (u p * waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u p) := by
  rw [waveDirDeriv_energyDensity hu p, hsolve p]

/-! ## The energy dominates the time derivative -/

/-- **The energy of a slice dominates the `L²` norm of the time derivative there.** This is what
bounds the source pairing in the inhomogeneous estimate. -/
theorem integral_sq_dirDeriv_le_waveEnergy
    (hsq : Integrable (fun x : Fin d → ℝ => (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u (t, x)) ^ 2)
      (volume : Measure (Fin d → ℝ)))
    (hden : Integrable (fun x : Fin d → ℝ => energyDensity u (t, x))
      (volume : Measure (Fin d → ℝ))) :
    (∫ x : Fin d → ℝ, (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u (t, x)) ^ 2) ≤ waveEnergy u t := by
  refine integral_mono hsq hden fun x => ?_
  have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ i : Fin d, (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u (t, x)) ^ 2 :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => sq_nonneg _

/-- **The energy of a slice dominates the `L²` norm of the field there.** -/

/-- **The energy flux identity for the inhomogeneous equation.** -/

/-!
# A quantitative Nyman–Beurling criterion, with explicit modulus

The three ingredients left open by the boundary/interior dichotomy assemble.

**(a) The space.**  Every Báez-Duarte generator is supported in `(0,1]`: for `t ≥ 1` both `1/t < 1`
and `θ/t < 1`, so `ρ_θ(t) = {θ/t} - θ{1/t} = θ/t - θ/t = 0`.  The target `1_{(0,1]}` is likewise
supported there.  The Mellin transform `f ↦ ∫₀¹ f(t)t^{-s}dt` therefore converges for `Re s < ½` and
maps `L²((0,1],dt)` unitarily onto the Hardy space `H²` of the half-plane `Re s < ½`, with the
Plancherel normalization

```text
‖f‖² = (1/2π) ∫_ℝ |f̂(½+iu)|² du ,
```

as the target itself confirms: `1̂(s) = 1/(1-s)`, whose boundary modulus squared integrates to `2π`,
matching `‖1_{(0,1]}‖² = 1`.

**(b) The vanishing constraint.**  The transform of a generator is `ζ(s)(n^{-s} - 1/n)/s`, so every
finite combination has transform `ζ(s)P(s)/s` with `P` entire.  At a zero `ρ` of `ζ` with `ρ ≠ 0`
this vanishes, and vanishing is preserved under `L²` limits because point evaluation in `H²` is
continuous.  The target does not vanish there: `1̂(ρ) = 1/(1-ρ) ≠ 0`.

**(c) The cost.**  With this normalization the diagonal kernel of `H²` of a half-plane is
`K(w,w) = 1/(2σ)`, `σ` the distance from `w` to the boundary line.  (The preceding module used the
unnormalized convention, where the constant is `1/(4πσ)`; the dichotomy is the same and only the
constant differs.)  The exact vanishing cost therefore gives, for a zero `ρ = β + iγ` of `ζ` with
`β < ½`,

```text
lim_N d_N  ≥  |1̂(ρ)| / √K(ρ,ρ)  =  √(1 - 2β) / |1 - ρ| .
```

By the functional equation the Riemann hypothesis fails exactly when such a `ρ` exists, so

> **If the Riemann hypothesis fails, the Báez-Duarte distances are bounded below by the explicit
> constant `√(1-2β)/|1-ρ|` for every zero `ρ` with `Re ρ < ½`.**

This is the quantitative form of the easy direction of the Nyman–Beurling criterion: not merely
`d_N ↛ 0`, but a modulus in the deviation.

**Universal height degradation.**  The constant is at most `1/|γ|`, since `√(1-2β) ≤ 1` and
`|1-ρ| ≥ |γ|`.  So a counterexample high up produces only a tiny floor, and combining the criterion
with numerical verification to height `X` would require the complementary analytic bound
`d_N ≤ 1/X` — with `d_N² ≍ 1/log N` that means `N ≥ exp(X²)`.  The same degradation appeared in the
flow lane, where verification to height `X` bounds `Λ` only by `π²/(2 log²X)`.  It is not an artefact
of either method:

> **Every quantified lane loses strength at a putative counterexample polynomially or exponentially
> in its height.  Numerical verification and analytic estimate never meet unless the analytic
> estimate is itself as strong as the verification height.**

That is the unified reason the "verify below, estimate above" architecture stalls, and it applies to
the Nyman–Beurling lane exactly as it does to the de Bruijn–Newman lane.

This file formalizes the kernel with the correct normalization, the explicit floor, and the height
degradation.
-/

open Real

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- The diagonal reproducing kernel of `H²` of a half-plane in the Plancherel normalization
`‖F‖² = (1/2π)∫|F|²`. -/
def nymanBeurlingHardyKernel (sigma : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 / (2 * sigma)

/-- **The explicit floor.**  The cost of vanishing at a point at distance `σ` from the boundary, for
a target of modulus `m` there, is `m·√(2σ)`. -/
def nbFloor (m sigma : ℝ) : ℝ := m * Real.sqrt (2 * sigma)

/-- The floor is the target modulus divided by the square root of the diagonal kernel. -/
theorem nbFloor_eq {m sigma : ℝ} (hs : 0 < sigma) :
    nbFloor m sigma = m / Real.sqrt (nymanBeurlingHardyKernel sigma) := by
  unfold nbFloor nymanBeurlingHardyKernel
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * sigma := by positivity
  rw [one_div, Real.sqrt_inv, div_inv_eq_mul]

/-- **Positivity.**  A zero strictly off the critical line gives a strictly positive floor. -/
theorem nbFloor_pos {m sigma : ℝ} (hm : 0 < m) (hs : 0 < sigma) : 0 < nbFloor m sigma := by
  unfold nbFloor
  have : 0 < Real.sqrt (2 * sigma) := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity)
  positivity

/-- **The floor in terms of the zero.**  With `σ = ½ - β` and `m = 1/|1-ρ|`, the floor is
`√(1-2β)/|1-ρ|`. -/
theorem nbFloor_of_zero (beta r : ℝ) :
    nbFloor (1 / r) (1 / 2 - beta) = Real.sqrt (1 - 2 * beta) / r := by
  unfold nbFloor
  have h2 : 2 * (1 / 2 - beta) = 1 - 2 * beta := by ring
  rw [h2, one_div, inv_mul_eq_div]

/-- **Height degradation.**  Since `√(1-2β) ≤ 1` for `β ≥ 0` and `|1-ρ| ≥ |γ|`, the floor is at most
`1/|γ|`: a counterexample high up gives only a tiny floor. -/
theorem nbFloor_le_inv_height {beta r g : ℝ} (hb0 : 0 ≤ beta)
    (hg : 0 < g) (hr : g ≤ r) :
    Real.sqrt (1 - 2 * beta) / r ≤ 1 / g := by
  have hrpos : 0 < r := lt_of_lt_of_le hg hr
  have hle : Real.sqrt (1 - 2 * beta) ≤ 1 := by
    have h1 : 1 - 2 * beta ≤ 1 := by linarith

/-!
# A perturbed oscillator in a general phase parameterization

The energy method for `w'' + (1 + q) w = 0` needs no privileged variable.  If `φ` is an increasing
phase and derivatives with respect to `φ` are written `Dw = w'/φ'`, `DDw = (Dw)'/φ'`, the same
three facts hold with `φ'` decorating each derivative:

```text
E = w² + (Dw)²,        E' = -2 φ' q w Dw,
A = w cos φ - Dw sin φ,   A' =  φ' q w sin φ,
B = w sin φ + Dw cos φ,   B' = -φ' q w cos φ.
```

If the perturbation obeys `|q| ≤ κ/φ²` then `E exp(κ/φ)` is antitone, because the drift integrates
to `∫ φ' κ/φ² = κ/φ`.

Working in the phase parameterization rather than in the phase variable avoids inverting `φ`
altogether: every statement is about functions of the original variable, and the change of
variables never has to be performed.
-/

noncomputable section

open Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

variable {w Dw DDw q φ Dφ : ℝ → ℝ}

/-- The oscillator energy in a phase parameterization. -/
def phaseEnergy (w Dw : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := w x ^ 2 + Dw x ^ 2

theorem phaseEnergy_nonneg (w Dw : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : 0 ≤ phaseEnergy w Dw x := by
  rw [phaseEnergy]
  positivity

/-- **The energy is almost conserved.**  The unperturbed contribution cancels exactly; what is left
is the perturbation times the phase speed. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_phaseEnergy {x : ℝ}
    (hw : HasDerivAt w (Dφ x * Dw x) x) (hDw : HasDerivAt Dw (Dφ x * DDw x) x)
    (hode : DDw x + (1 + q x) * w x = 0) :
    HasDerivAt (phaseEnergy w Dw) (-(2 * Dφ x * q x * (w x * Dw x))) x := by
  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun v : ℝ => w v ^ 2) (2 * w x * (Dφ x * Dw x)) x := by
    have h := hw.pow 2
    have hv : ((2 : ℕ) : ℝ) * w x ^ (2 - 1) * (Dφ x * Dw x)
        = 2 * w x * (Dφ x * Dw x) := by norm_num
    rw [hv] at h
    exact h
  have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun v : ℝ => Dw v ^ 2) (2 * Dw x * (Dφ x * DDw x)) x := by
    have h := hDw.pow 2
    have hv : ((2 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Dw x ^ (2 - 1) * (Dφ x * DDw x)
        = 2 * Dw x * (Dφ x * DDw x) := by norm_num
    rw [hv] at h
    exact h
  have h := h1.add h2
  have hval : 2 * w x * (Dφ x * Dw x) + 2 * Dw x * (Dφ x * DDw x)
      = -(2 * Dφ x * q x * (w x * Dw x)) := by
    have hsec : DDw x = -((1 + q x) * w x) := by linarith
    rw [hsec]
    ring
  rw [hval] at h
  exact h

/-- **The differential inequality**, by the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality. -/
theorem abs_deriv_phaseEnergy_le {x κ : ℝ} (hDφ : 0 ≤ Dφ x)
    (hq : |q x| ≤ κ / φ x ^ 2) :
    |-(2 * Dφ x * q x * (w x * Dw x))| ≤ Dφ x * (κ / φ x ^ 2) * phaseEnergy w Dw x := by
  have hamgm : 2 * |w x| * |Dw x| ≤ w x ^ 2 + Dw x ^ 2 := by
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (|w x| - |Dw x|), sq_abs (w x), sq_abs (Dw x)]
  have hκ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ κ / φ x ^ 2 := le_trans (abs_nonneg _) hq
  rw [abs_neg, abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_mul, phaseEnergy, abs_mul (w x) (Dw x),
    abs_of_nonneg hDφ]
  have habs : |(2 : ℝ)| = 2 := by norm_num
  rw [habs]
  have hnn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ |w x| * |Dw x| := by positivity
  calc 2 * Dφ x * |q x| * (|w x| * |Dw x|)
      ≤ 2 * Dφ x * (κ / φ x ^ 2) * (|w x| * |Dw x|) := by
        have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hq (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Dφ x)
        nlinarith [hnn]
    _ ≤ Dφ x * (κ / φ x ^ 2) * (w x ^ 2 + Dw x ^ 2) := by
        nlinarith [hamgm, mul_nonneg hDφ hκ]

/-- The cosine coefficient against the unperturbed basis in the phase. -/
def phaseCosCoeff (w Dw φ : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := w x * Real.cos (φ x) - Dw x * Real.sin (φ x)

/-- The sine coefficient. -/
def phaseSinCoeff (w Dw φ : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := w x * Real.sin (φ x) + Dw x * Real.cos (φ x)

/-- **The exact two-branch representation.** -/
theorem phase_eq_coeff (w Dw φ : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) :
    w x = phaseCosCoeff w Dw φ x * Real.cos (φ x)
      + phaseSinCoeff w Dw φ x * Real.sin (φ x) := by
  rw [phaseCosCoeff, phaseSinCoeff]
  linear_combination (-(w x)) * Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq (φ x)

/-- The coefficients carry exactly the energy. -/
theorem phaseCoeff_sq_add (w Dw φ : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) :
    phaseCosCoeff w Dw φ x ^ 2 + phaseSinCoeff w Dw φ x ^ 2 = phaseEnergy w Dw x := by
  rw [phaseCosCoeff, phaseSinCoeff, phaseEnergy]
  nlinarith [Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq (φ x)]

theorem hasDerivAt_phaseCosCoeff {x : ℝ}
    (hφ : HasDerivAt φ (Dφ x) x)
    (hw : HasDerivAt w (Dφ x * Dw x) x) (hDw : HasDerivAt Dw (Dφ x * DDw x) x)
    (hode : DDw x + (1 + q x) * w x = 0) :
    HasDerivAt (phaseCosCoeff w Dw φ) (Dφ x * q x * w x * Real.sin (φ x)) x := by
  have hc : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Real.cos (φ t)) (-Real.sin (φ x) * Dφ x) x :=
    (Real.hasDerivAt_cos (φ x)).comp x hφ
  have hs : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Real.sin (φ t)) (Real.cos (φ x) * Dφ x) x :=
    (Real.hasDerivAt_sin (φ x)).comp x hφ
  have h := (hw.mul hc).sub (hDw.mul hs)
  have hval : Dφ x * Dw x * Real.cos (φ x) + w x * (-Real.sin (φ x) * Dφ x)
      - (Dφ x * DDw x * Real.sin (φ x) + Dw x * (Real.cos (φ x) * Dφ x))
      = Dφ x * q x * w x * Real.sin (φ x) := by
    have hsec : DDw x = -((1 + q x) * w x) := by linarith
    rw [hsec]

/-!
# Polynomial moments of literal coprime deletion polygons

For actual moduli `P=p+1` and `Q=q+1`, join the successive prefix endpoints
`(n mod P,n mod Q)` by straight segments. Their velocities are exactly the existing
Euler-deletion coefficients, and one common period is a closed polygon.

CRT factors every polynomial segment density into two explicit one-coordinate phase sums.
All coefficient-degree-at-most-three polynomial one-forms have zero circulation. The
higher moment `integral x*y^3 dx` is exactly `P*(P-1)*Q*(Q-1)*(Q-2)/120` for coprime
`P,Q`. In particular the literal moduli-2-and-3 path gives the closed value `1/10`.

This is a finite unweighted arithmetic statement. It supplies no assertion about a weighted
infinite product, no vanishing at a zeta zero, and no RH implication. Polynomial-moment
and path-signature methods have published ancestry; no global novelty claim is made here.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
namespace RHTower.DeletionJointPolygon
noncomputable section

/-- Velocity of the literal modulus `p+1` deletion path. -/
def velocity (p n : ℕ) : ℝ := blockDeletionCoefficient (p+1) (n+1)

/-- Straight interpolation of the exact residue-valued prefix. -/
def position (p n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := (n % (p+1) : ℕ) + t * velocity p n

/-- Polynomial one-form integrated along one full common period. -/
def circulation (p q a b : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range ((p+1)*(q+1)),
    position p n t ^ a * position q n t ^ b * velocity p n

/-- Position moments across one coordinate's phases. -/
def phaseMoment (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range p, ((j:ℝ)+t)^k) + ((p:ℝ)*(1-t))^k

/-- Velocity-weighted position moments across one coordinate's phases. -/
def velocityMoment (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range p, ((j:ℝ)+t)^k) - (p:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*(1-t))^k

theorem velocity_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : n < p) : velocity p n = 1 := by
  have hd : ¬ p+1 ∣ n+1 := Nat.not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt (Nat.succ_pos n)
    (Nat.succ_lt_succ hn)
  simp [velocity, blockDeletionCoefficient, hd]

theorem velocity_last (p : ℕ) : velocity p p = -(p:ℝ) := by
  simp [velocity, blockDeletionCoefficient]

theorem position_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : n < p) (t : ℝ) :
    position p n t = (n:ℝ)+t := by
  simp [position, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hn), velocity_of_lt hn]

theorem position_last (p : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : position p p t = (p:ℝ)*(1-t) := by
  simp only [position, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.lt_succ_self p), velocity_last]
  ring

theorem velocity_periodic (p : ℕ) : Function.Periodic (velocity p) (p+1) := by
  intro n
  exact congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z:ℝ))
    (DeletionCoprimeWords.shifted_deletion_periodic (p+1) n)

theorem position_periodic (p : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    Function.Periodic (fun n => position p n t) (p+1) := by
  intro n
  simp only [position, Nat.add_mod_right, velocity_periodic p n]

theorem sum_position_pow (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (p+1), position p n t ^ k) = phaseMoment p k t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, position_last]
  unfold phaseMoment
  congr 1
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun n hn => by rw [position_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn)])

theorem sum_position_pow_velocity (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (p+1), position p n t ^ k * velocity p n) =
      velocityMoment p k t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, position_last, velocity_last]
  unfold velocityMoment
  have hs : (∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, position p n t ^ k * velocity p n) =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, ((n:ℝ)+t)^k := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro n hn
    rw [position_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn), velocity_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn), mul_one]
  rw [hs]
  ring

/-- The starting coordinate is the actual sum of previous deletion jumps. -/
theorem position_zero_eq_prefix (p n : ℕ) :
    position p n 0 = (deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) n : ℝ) := by
  simp only [position, zero_mul, add_zero, deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod, Int.cast_natCast]

/-- Consecutive straight segments meet at their endpoints. -/
theorem segment_endpoint (p n : ℕ) : position p n 1 = position p (n+1) 0 := by
  have h : deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) n + blockDeletionCoefficient (p+1) (n+1) =
      deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) (n+1) := by
    exact (Finset.sum_range_succ _ _).symm
  rw [deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod, deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod] at h
  have hr := congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z:ℝ)) h
  simpa only [position, velocity, one_mul, zero_mul, add_zero, Int.cast_add, Int.cast_natCast] using hr

/-- A common period returns both literal coordinates to the origin. -/
theorem common_period_closed (p q : ℕ) :
    position p ((p+1)*(q+1)) 0 = 0 ∧ position q ((p+1)*(q+1)) 0 = 0 := by
  simp [position]

/-- CRT factors the actual segment integrand; no averaging approximation is used. -/

fun _ => restrictInteractionPacket active z) := by
    intro states
    induction states using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty =>
        unfold FormalMultilinearSeries.coeff
        rfl
    | @insert active states hactive ih =>
        rw [Finset.sum_insert hactive, Finset.sum_insert hactive]
        unfold FormalMultilinearSeries.coeff at ih ⊢
        rw [FormalMultilinearSeries.add_apply,
          FormalMultilinearSeries.smul_apply,
          _root_.add_apply,
          _root_.smul_apply]
        rw [FormalMultilinearSeries.compContinuousLinearMap_apply]
        simp only [smul_eq_mul]
        have hone :
            (⇑(scalarRayCLM (restrictInteractionPacket active z)) ∘
                (1 : Fin n → ℂ)) =
              (fun _ : Fin n => restrictInteractionPacket active z) := by
          funext i
          simp [Function.comp_apply]
        rw [hone]
        change
          mu ℂ active packet *
                series n (fun _ => restrictInteractionPacket active z) +
              ((∑ x ∈ states,
                  (mu ℂ x packet) •
                    series.compContinuousLinearMap
                      (scalarRayCLM (restrictInteractionPacket x z))) n) 1 =
            mu ℂ active packet *
                series n (fun _ => restrictInteractionPacket active z) +
              ∑ x ∈ states,
                mu ℂ x packet *
                  series n (fun _ => restrictInteractionPacket x z)
        rw [ih]
  rw [packetRaySeries, hsum]
  rfl

/-- A scalar analytic response is active when it is not the zero germ. -/
def AnalyticSectorActive (f : ℂ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ¬f =ᶠ[𝓝 0] (fun _ : ℂ => 0)

/-- Exact analytic birth depth of a scalar response represented by `series`. -/
noncomputable def analyticBirthOrder
    (series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ) : ℕ :=
  series.order

/-- Analytic unit left after removing the exact birth monomial. -/
noncomputable def analyticBirthUnit
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) (series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ) : ℂ → ℂ :=
  (Function.swap dslope 0)^[series.order] f

/-- An active analytic germ cannot have the zero Taylor series. -/
theorem series_ne_zero_of_analyticSectorActive
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0)
    (hactive : AnalyticSectorActive f) :
    series ≠ 0 := by
  intro hzero
  apply hactive
  exact HasFPowerSeriesAt.eventually_eq_zero (by simpa [hzero] using hf)

/-- An active response vanishing at zero has positive birth depth. -/
theorem analyticBirthOrder_pos
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0)
    (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (hactive : AnalyticSectorActive f) :
    0 < analyticBirthOrder series := by
  have hseries := series_ne_zero_of_analyticSectorActive hf hactive
  have hcoeff0 : series.coeff 0 = 0 := by
    simpa [hf0] using hf.coeff_zero 1
  have hseries0 : series 0 = 0 :=
    FormalMultilinearSeries.coeff_eq_zero.mp hcoeff0
  apply Nat.pos_of_ne_zero
  intro horder
  have hnonzero := FormalMultilinearSeries.apply_order_ne_zero hseries
  rw [analyticBirthOrder] at horder
  rw [horder] at hnonzero
  exact hnonzero hseries0

/-- Coefficient at the exact birth depth is nonzero. -/
theorem analyticBirthCoefficient_ne_zero
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0)
    (hactive : AnalyticSectorActive f) :
    series series.order ≠ 0 :=
  FormalMultilinearSeries.apply_order_ne_zero
    (series_ne_zero_of_analyticSectorActive hf hactive)

/-- Every coefficient below exact birth depth vanishes. -/
theorem analyticBirthCoefficient_eq_zero_below
    (series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n < analyticBirthOrder series) :
    series n = 0 :=
  FormalMultilinearSeries.apply_eq_zero_of_lt_order
    (by simpa [analyticBirthOrder] using hn)

/-- The factor left after removing the exact birth monomial is analytic. -/
theorem analyticBirthUnit_analyticAt
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ (analyticBirthUnit f series) 0 := by
  exact
    (hf.has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope series.order).analyticAt

/-- The analytic birth unit is nonzero at the uncoupled point. -/
theorem analyticBirthUnit_zero_ne
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0)
    (hactive : AnalyticSectorActive f) :
    analyticBirthUnit f series 0 ≠ 0 := by
  exact hf.iterate_dslope_fslope_ne_zero
    (series_ne_zero_of_analyticSectorActive hf hactive)

/-- **Exact analytic birth factorization.** Every active analytic response
is its birth monomial times a nonvanishing analytic unit. -/
theorem analytic_eq_pow_birthOrder_mul_birthUnit
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0) (g : ℂ) :
    f g =
      g ^ analyticBirthOrder series * analyticBirthUnit f series g := by
  simpa [analyticBirthOrder, analyticBirthUnit, smul_eq_mul] using

ed on the all-one direction is nonzero. -/
theorem formalMultilinearSeries_ne_zero_iff_exists_apply_one_ne
    (series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ) :
    series ≠ 0 ↔ ∃ n, series n (fun _ => 1) ≠ 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hne
    by_contra hall
    push Not at hall
    apply hne
    ext n
    rw [← (series n).mkPiRing_apply_one_eq_self]
    simp [hall n]
  · rintro ⟨n, hn⟩ hzero
    exact hn (by simp [hzero])

/-- Character activity in the spectral-jet filtration is exactly
nonvanishing of its analytic relation series. -/
theorem spectralCharacterActive_iff_characterSeries_ne_zero
    {I : Type*}
    (series : I → FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ)
    (k : ProjectiveCharacter I) :
    SpectralCharacterActive (spectralTaylorJet series) k ↔
      projectiveCharacterSeries series k ≠ 0 := by
  rw [formalMultilinearSeries_ne_zero_iff_exists_apply_one_ne]
  unfold SpectralCharacterActive
  constructor <;> rintro ⟨n, hn⟩ <;> refine ⟨n, ?_⟩
  · rwa [projectiveCharacterSeries_apply_one_eq_relationJet]
  · rwa [projectiveCharacterSeries_apply_one_eq_relationJet] at hn

/-- Exact filtration birth equals the analytic order of the character's
detuning series. -/
theorem spectralCharacterBirthOrder_eq_series_order
    {I : Type*}
    (series : I → FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ)
    (k : ProjectiveCharacter I)
    (hactive : SpectralCharacterActive (spectralTaylorJet series) k) :
    spectralCharacterBirthOrder (spectralTaylorJet series) k hactive =
      (projectiveCharacterSeries series k).order := by
  let p := projectiveCharacterSeries series k
  have hp : p ≠ 0 :=
    (spectralCharacterActive_iff_characterSeries_ne_zero series k).mp
      hactive
  have hpOrderApply : p p.order (fun _ => 1) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hzero
    apply FormalMultilinearSeries.apply_order_ne_zero hp
    rw [← (p p.order).mkPiRing_apply_one_eq_self]
    rw [hzero, ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiRing_zero]
  have hrelationOrder :
      projectiveSpectralRelationJet
          (spectralTaylorJet series) p.order k ≠ 0 := by
    rwa [← projectiveCharacterSeries_apply_one_eq_relationJet]
  have hle :
      spectralCharacterBirthOrder
          (spectralTaylorJet series) k hactive ≤ p.order :=
    Nat.find_min' hactive hrelationOrder
  apply le_antisymm hle
  by_contra hnot
  have hlt :
      spectralCharacterBirthOrder
          (spectralTaylorJet series) k hactive < p.order := by
    omega
  have hpzero :
      p (spectralCharacterBirthOrder
          (spectralTaylorJet series) k hactive) = 0 :=
    FormalMultilinearSeries.apply_eq_zero_of_lt_order hlt
  have hrelationZero :
      projectiveSpectralRelationJet
          (spectralTaylorJet series)
          (spectralCharacterBirthOrder
            (spectralTaylorJet series) k hactive) k = 0 := by
    rw [← projectiveCharacterSeries_apply_one_eq_relationJet]
    simp [p, hpzero]
  exact spectralRelationJet_birthOrder_ne_zero hactive hrelationZero

/-- **Every finite character of every analytic spectrum has universal wall
crossing.** The ambient spectral label type can be arbitrary. -/
theorem projectiveCharacter_wallCrossing
    {I : Type*} (energy : I → ℂ → ℂ)
    (series : I → FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ)
    (henergy : ∀ i, HasFPowerSeriesAt (energy i) (series i) 0)
    (k : ProjectiveCharacter I)
    (hactive : SpectralCharacterActive (spectralTaylorJet series) k)
    {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 0 < τ) :
    let b := spectralCharacterBirthOrder
      (spectralTaylorJet series) k hactive
    let response := projectiveCharacterResponse energy k
    (∀ r < b,
      Tendsto
        (fun g : ℝ => Real.sinc (τ * (‖response g‖ / g ^ r)))
        (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)) ∧
    Tendsto
      (fun g : ℝ => Real.sinc (τ * (‖response g‖ / g ^ b)))
      (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 (Real.sinc
        (τ * ‖analyticBirthUnit response
          (projectiveCharacterSeries series k) 0‖))) ∧
    (∀ r, b < r →
      Tendsto
        (fun g : ℝ => Real.sinc (τ * (‖response g‖ / g ^ r)))
        (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) := by
  dsimp only
  have hf :=
    hasFPowerSeriesAt_projectiveCharacterResponse
      energy series henergy k
  have hseries :
      projectiveCharacterSeries series k ≠ 0 :=
    (spectralCharacterActive_iff_characterSeries_ne_zero series k).mp
      hactive
  have hresponse : AnalyticSectorActive
      (projectiveCharacterResponse energy k) :=
    by
      intro hzero
      exact hseries (hf.eq_zero_of_eventually hzero)
  have hwall :=
    analyticSectorReporter_wallCrossing hf hresponse hτ
  have hbirth :=
    spectralCharacterBirthOrder_eq_series_order series k hactive
  simpa [analyticBirthOrder, hbirth] using hwall

/-!
# Analytic order rigidity from asymptotic onset

An analytic function that is `O (‖g‖ ^ r)` cannot have a nonzero Taylor
coefficient below order `r`. This closes the exact bridge from geometric
Big-O locality bounds to intrinsic analytic birth valuation.
-/

open Filter Topology Asymptotics

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Analytic unit obtained after removing the exact series-order monomial. -/
private def analyticOrderUnit
    (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ) : ℂ → ℂ :=
  (Function.swap dslope 0)^[series.order] f

private theorem analyticOrderUnit_zero_ne
    {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0)
    (hseries : series ≠ 0) :
    analyticOrderUnit f series 0 ≠ 0 := by
  exact hf.iterate_dslope_fslope_ne_zero hseries

private theorem analyticOrderUnit_continuousAt
    {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0) :
    ContinuousAt (analyticOrderUnit f series) 0 := by
  exact
    (hf.has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope
      series.order).analyticAt.continuousAt

private theorem analytic_eq_pow_order_mul_unit
    {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0)
    (g : ℂ) :
    f g =
      g ^ series.order *
        analyticOrderUnit f series g := by
  simpa [analyticOrderUnit, smul_eq_mul] using
    hf.eq_pow_order_mul_iterate_dslope g

private theorem tendsto_norm_div_norm_pow_order
    {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    {series : FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ}
    (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f series 0) :
    Tendsto
      (fun g : ℂ =>
        ‖f g‖ / ‖g‖ ^ series.order)
      (𝓝[≠] 0)
      (𝓝 ‖analyticOrderUnit f series 0‖) := by
  have hunit :
      Tendsto
        (fun g : ℂ =>
          ‖analyticOrderUnit f series g‖)
        (𝓝[≠] 0)
        (𝓝 ‖analyticOrderUnit f series 0‖) :=
    (analyticOrderUnit_continuousAt hf).norm.mono_left
      inf_le_left
  apply hunit.congr'
  filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with g hg
  have hg0 : g ≠ 0 := by
    simpa using hg

    norm_mul, norm_pow]

source_arguments.statement:
theorem suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimePairFloor_sqrt_lower
    {n : ℕ} (hn : Real.exp 20 ≤ (n : ℝ)) :
    Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (1024 * Real.sqrt 20) ≤
      (((_root_.RHTower.suzukiMangoldtFivePrimeBlock n).card / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) *
        (suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor n / 8)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimePairFloor_sqrt_lower
    {n : ℕ} (hn : Real.exp 20 ≤ (n : ℝ)) :
    Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (1024 * Real.sqrt 20) ≤
      (((_root_.RHTower.suzukiMangoldtFivePrimeBlock n).card / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) *
        (suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor n / 8)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let m := (_root_.RHTower.suzukiMangoldtFivePrimeBlock n).card
  let q := m / 2
  let L2 := Real.log (2 * (n : ℝ))
  let L5 := Real.log (5 * (n : ℝ))
  have hnPos : (0 : ℝ) < n := (Real.exp_pos 20).trans_le hn
  have hL2 : 0 < L2 := Real.log_pos (by
    have hnNat : 0 < n := by exact_mod_cast hnPos
    exact_mod_cast (show 1 < 2 * n by omega))
  have hL5 : 0 < L5 := Real.log_pos (by
    have hnNat : 0 < n := by exact_mod_cast hnPos
    exact_mod_cast (show 1 < 5 * n by omega))
  have hm := suzukiMangoldtFivePrimeBlock_card_lower hn
  have hq := suzukiMangoldtFivePrimeBlock_card_quarter_le_div_two hn
  have hqLower : (n : ℝ) / (16 * L5) ≤ (q : ℝ) := by
    dsimp [m, q, L5] at hm hq ⊢
    calc
      (n : ℝ) / (16 * Real.log (5 * (n : ℝ))) =
          ((n : ℝ) / (4 * Real.log (5 * (n : ℝ)))) / 4 := by ring
      _ ≤ ((_root_.RHTower.suzukiMangoldtFivePrimeBlock n).card : ℝ) / 4 :=
        div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hm (by norm_num)
      _ ≤ _ := hq
  have hsquare : 5 * (n : ℝ) ≤ (2 * (n : ℝ)) ^ 2 := by
    have hnFive : (5 : ℝ) ≤ n := by
      nlinarith [Real.add_one_le_exp (20 : ℝ)]
    nlinarith
  have hlogRatio : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ L2 / L5 := by
    have hlog : L5 ≤ 2 * L2 := by
      have h := Real.log_le_log (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) < 5 * n) hsquare
      dsimp [L2, L5]
      rw [Real.log_pow] at h
      norm_num at h ⊢
      exact h
    rw [le_div_iff₀ hL5]
    nlinarith
  have hdelta0 := suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor_nonneg hn
  have hqdelta : ((n : ℝ) / (16 * L5)) *
      (suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor n / 8) ≤
        (q : ℝ) * (suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor n / 8) :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hqLower (div_nonneg hdelta0 (by norm_num))
  have hsqrtN : 0 < Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hnPos
  have hsqrt20 : 0 < Real.sqrt (20 : ℝ) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by norm_num)
  have hsqrtMul : Real.sqrt (20 * (n : ℝ)) =
      Real.sqrt 20 * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) := by
    rw [Real.sqrt_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 20)]
  have hrewrite : ((n : ℝ) / (16 * L5)) *
      (suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor n / 8) =
        (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (512 * Real.sqrt 20)) * (L2 / L5) := by
    rw [suzukiPositiveSharedPlaneTwentyPrimeFloor]
    dsimp [L2]
    rw [hsqrtMul]
    field_simp [hL5.ne', hsqrtN.ne', hsqrt20.ne']
    rw [Real.sq_sqrt hnPos.le]
    ring
  have hscale0 : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (512 * Real.sqrt 20) := by positivity
  have hmain : Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (1024 * Real.sqrt 20) ≤
      (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (512 * Real.sqrt 20)) * (L2 / L5) := by
    have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlogRatio hscale0
    calc
      Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (1024 * Real.sqrt 20) =
          (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / (512 * Real.sqrt 20)) * (1 / 2) := by ring
      _ ≤ _ := h
  rw [hrewrite] at hqdelta
  dsimp [q, m] at hqdelta ⊢
  exact hmain.trans hqdelta

### 2.5 Fibred multi-coefficient obstruction doctrine `O`

No single abelian group can retain all corpus obstructions, but an unstructured list would merely
recreate the rejected organ bag. The regular core is a stable bivariant coefficient stack

\[
 \mathcal H:\mathbb B_{\rm reg}\longrightarrow\mathsf{Pr}^{L}_{\rm st}

\]

carrying pullback, pushforward, localization triangles, duality, and canonical exchange maps.
Exact realization functors `rho_alpha:H->C_alpha` read homological, `K`-theoretic, Witt, cyclic,
or pro-derived shadows. More generally let `Coeff` index these realizations and

\[
 q:\mathfrak D\longrightarrow\mathsf{Coeff}
 \tag{NGD.2c}
\]

a fibration whose fibre `D_alpha` is the target of coefficient theory `alpha`. Morphisms in
`Coeff` are named transition functors--forgetful maps, completion, Chern characters, index maps,
or associated gradeds--with coherence. `O` assigns a presentation-invariant
exchange defect as a compatible section/diagram. Nonstable modalities and numerical valuations
remain typed but are not mislabeled as stable coefficient theories:

| Layer | Examples | Corpus shadows |
|---|---|---|
| stable/exact realization | relative cohomology, pro-derived relations, Grothendieck--Witt, equivariant `K`/cyclic, Rees type | transgression, Hedenmalm/Gelfand defects, Stokes inertia, Real-corona, rank transmutation |

Comparison between coefficient theories must be a named functor or pairing. Calling two shadows
"the same obstruction" without such a map is forbidden. A shadow family that violates transition

logarithmic current, derivation, relative cycle, anomaly, port charge, or pro-class. It is

nonvanishing is imposed. `tau` is a fixed natural transgression from its source coefficient theory

The corpus already contains exact examples: Möbius inversion, von Mangoldt logarithmic current,

# EDQ full-source logarithmic saving

Stage: 3-formalized. [BRIDGE] derived theorem; dependency-closed paper proof and Lean proof complete.
Full chain: Euler deletion → exact complex zero balance → signed arithmetic separation → exclusion of off-line zeros → RH.
Objective: derive an unconditional upper bound on the complete arithmetic energy and signed Gram cross sum, using actual Möbius cancellation with the entire tail retained.

## Paper proof

Let M(k)=sum_(d<=k) mu(d), H_N=sum_(d<=N) mu(d)/d, and A_N(n)
be the literal unweighted deletion primitive (negative modular approximant).
Suppose N,L>=1 and abs(M(k))<=epsilon*k for every k>=N.
For N<n<=N*L the omitted floor sum is
sum_(N<d<=n) mu(d)*floor(n/d).
Its coefficient prefixes M(N+j)-M(N) have absolute value at most
2*epsilon*n. Its nonnegative floor weight decreases, starting at no
more than L. Finite Abel summation bounds this whole signed sum by
2*epsilon*n*L. The exact global residual identity therefore gives,
for every 1<=n<=N*L,
abs(A_N(n))<=1+n*(abs(H_N)+2*epsilon*L).
The known exact initial identity covers n<=N.

Put b=abs(H_N)+2*epsilon*L. On the first T=N*L coordinates,
abs(A_N(n))^2/n^2 <=2/n^2+2*b^2. The full inverse-square sum is
at most 2. Beyond T use abs(A_N(n))<=N and the inverse-square tail
bound 1/T. Genuine fixed-cutoff summability then gives the full estimate
E_N <=4+2*N*L*b^2+N/L.
The modular carrier norm squared is at most E_N by termwise comparison
of 1/(n(n+1)) with 1/n^2. Together with the existing reverse estimate,
norm(rawVec_N)^2 <= E_N <= 2*norm(rawVec_N)^2. Its signed cross sum is
at most that norm squared because the complete diagonal is nonnegative;
in absolute value it is at most E_N plus that diagonal.

For any prescribed q, put r=q+1, P=(log N)^r and L=floor(P).
Eventually P>=2, P/2<=L<=P. The corpus gives a constant C>=0 such
that, for all k>=N, abs(M(k))<=C*k/(log N)^(2*r); it also gives
abs(H_N)<=1/(log N)^(2*r) eventually. Set epsilon=C/P^2.
Then b<=(1+2*C)/P, so the finite energy bound is at most
4+(2*(1+2*C)^2+2)*N/P. Eventually P<=N, hence E_N<=B*N/P
for one fixed B. The diagonal is eventually at most 4*log N, which is
absorbed by 4*N/P. This supplies arbitrary logarithmic savings relative
to N, unconditionally, for the full energy, full modular norm, and
absolute signed cross sum. Each of these quantities times (log N)^q/N
tends to zero for every natural q. The existing actual-zero current
transfer gives the same limit for abs(Re Q_N(rho)) at every actual zero.
No part of the infinite tail is dropped.

## Remaining gap

N divided by any fixed logarithmic power still grows faster than every
fixed logarithmic power. These source upper bounds therefore coexist
with the already proved superlogarithmic escape at hypothetical off-line
zeros. They are actual producer estimates, but do not supply the cofinal
polynomial-log ceiling required by the EDQ RH receiver. No RH conclusion
or off-line zero existence is asserted.

to pivot generation is exact:

```text
y belongs to the embedded differential field C<g_1,...,g_d>
    iff
v belongs to span_C{u_1,...,u_d}.
```

The complementary statement is stronger than non-membership:

```text
y is differentially algebraically independent over C<g_1,...,g_d>
    iff
v does not belong to span_C{u_1,...,u_d}.
```

Thus every new profile direction contributes a genuinely relative hypertranscendental generator,
not merely a new element of the ambient field.

Consequently, for any finite source family `x` and any linearly independent pivot family `y`,

```text
C<x> is contained in C<y>
    iff
span(profile(x)) is contained in span(profile(y)).
```

In particular, two finite linearly independent prime-radial presentations generate the same
embedded differential field exactly when their profile subspaces are equal.  The profile span is
therefore a complete invariant of both membership and generated-field equality on minimal finite
presentations.  This resolves the simultaneous-family question left open by independence-only
results: distinct presentations may generate the same field, but only through ordinary linear
change of profile coordinates.

The classification also preserves intersections in basis-decomposition form.  Let `a` be a common
profile basis, let `b` and `c` be complementary profile blocks, and assume the combined family
`a ⊕ b ⊕ c` is linearly independent.  Then

```text
C<a,b> ∩ C<a,c> = C<a>.
```

There are therefore no hidden common differential observables beyond the common profile
subspace.  The proof uses the classical linear-disjointness of rational-function fields only as
infrastructure; the prime-valuation rank law is what identifies the actual embedded fields to
which that meet theorem applies.

## Stronger arbitrary-tail certificate

The proof establishes a theorem beyond the prime-radial class.  Let `g_1,...,g_d` be arbitrary
sources supported on positive prime powers, with no restriction on unselected valuation layers.
If there are pairwise-distinct exponents `e_1,...,e_d` for which the profile minor

```text
P(i,j) = g_j(p^(e_i+1))
```

is independent of `p` and nonsingular, then the sources are differentially independent.  Thus
uncontrolled infinite prime-power tails cannot cancel a nonsingular finite valuation minor.

## Proof geometry

For a finite jet rectangle, linear independence of the profiles supplies a nonsingular evaluation
minor at pairwise-distinct valuation coordinates.  Distinct packets of primes supply independent
logarithmic clocks inside every selected valuation row.  Applying prime derivations to the jets
produces an arithmetic-function Jacobian whose rows may have arbitrary infinite tails along their
own prime rays.

Unique factorization isolates one coefficient of the full convolution determinant:

```text
coefficient at product_i q_i^(e_i)
    = determinant of the rowwise scalar coefficient matrix.
```

The scalar determinant is a block product of the valuation-profile minor and logarithmic-clock

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.EntireWeightedLittlewoodLeftClosure
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.JensenMeanLog

/-!
# From Littlewood's rectangle identity to a zero count

Levinson's method bounds the number of zeros of a detector to the right of an abscissa `σ` by
Littlewood's weighted zero-mass identity: a zero with real part at least `σ` carries horizontal
weight at least `σ − c` in that identity, so the whole count is controlled by the boundary data of
the rectangle `[c,d] × [T₁,T₂]`.

Two of the four boundary terms are left as they stand (the horizontal edges and the logarithmic
derivative on the right edge, both `O(log T)` in the application).  The other two are estimated
here: the *left*-edge logarithmic integral is bounded above by Jensen's inequality against the mean
square on that edge, and the right-edge logarithmic integral is bounded below by a pointwise lower
bound for `‖f‖`.  The output is exactly the shape Levinson's method consumes,

```text
2π (σ − c) · #{zeros with Re ≥ σ}
    ≤ ½(T₂−T₁)·log( mean square on Re s = c )  −  (T₂−T₁)·log A  +  edges.
```

Zeros on the left edge are permitted throughout: they carry zero weight in the identity, and the
logarithmic integral of an entire function on a vertical segment always converges.
-/

open Complex MeasureTheory Set Filter intervalIntegral Topology
open scoped Interval

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The logarithmic norm of an entire function is interval integrable on every vertical segment,
zeros on the segment included. -/
theorem intervalIntegrable_log_norm_vertical_of_entire
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f Set.univ) (a T₁ T₂ : ℝ) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => Real.log ‖f ((a : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I)‖) volume T₁ T₂ := by
  apply MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log_norm
  intro t _
  have hpath : AnalyticAt ℝ (fun u : ℝ => (a : ℂ) + (u : ℂ) * I) t :=
    analyticAt_const.add ((Complex.ofRealCLM.analyticAt t).mul analyticAt_const)
  exact AnalyticAt.comp (f := fun u : ℝ => (a : ℂ) + (u : ℂ) * I)
    (hf _ (Set.mem_univ _)).restrictScalars hpath |>.meromorphicAt

/-- Jensen's logarithmic mean-value step, with the nonvanishing hypothesis relaxed to a null
exceptional set. -/
theorem two_mul_integral_log_norm_le_ae {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) {f : ℝ → ℂ}
    (hne : ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Set.Icc a b)), f t ≠ 0)
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => ‖f t‖ ^ 2) volume a b)
    (hlogint : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => Real.log ‖f t‖) volume a b)
    (hpos : 0 < ∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2) :
    2 * (∫ t in a..b, Real.log ‖f t‖)
      ≤ (b - a) * Real.log ((∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2) / (b - a)) := by
  have hlen : (0 : ℝ) < b - a := by linarith
  set C : ℝ := (∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2) / (b - a) with hC
  have hC0 : 0 < C := div_pos hpos hlen
  have hmono : (∫ t in a..b, 2 * Real.log ‖f t‖)
      ≤ ∫ t in a..b, (‖f t‖ ^ 2 / C + Real.log C - 1) := by
    refine intervalIntegral.integral_mono_ae_restrict hab.le (hlogint.const_mul 2)
      (((hint.div_const C).add intervalIntegrable_const).sub intervalIntegrable_const) ?_
    filter_upwards [hne] with t ht
    have hn : 0 < ‖f t‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr ht
    have hu : 0 < ‖f t‖ ^ 2 := by positivity
    have h := log_le_div_add_log_sub_one hu hC0
    rw [Real.log_pow] at h
    push_cast at h
    exact h
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul] at hmono
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_sub ((hint.div_const C).add intervalIntegrable_const)
      intervalIntegrable_const, intervalIntegral.integral_add (hint.div_const C)
      intervalIntegrable_const, intervalIntegral.integral_div] at hmono
  simp only [intervalIntegral.integral_const, smul_eq_mul] at hmono
  have hcancel : (∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2) / C = b - a := by
    rw [hC]; field_simp
  rw [hcancel] at hmono
  linarith

/-- Positive interior sample plus continuity and global nonnegativity gives a positive interval
integral. -/
theorem intervalIntegral_pos_of_continuous_global_nonneg {g : ℝ → ℝ} {A B : ℝ}
    (hg : Continuous g) (hnonneg : ∀ t, 0 ≤ g t)
    (hposn : ∃ t ∈ Set.Ioo A B, 0 < g t) :
    0 < ∫ t in A..B, g t := by
  obtain ⟨t₀, ht₀, htpos⟩ := hposn
  have hAB : A < B := lt_trans ht₀.1 ht₀.2
  have hgi : IntervalIntegrable g volume A B := hg.intervalIntegrable A B
  have hnonneg_ae : 0 ≤ᶠ[ae (volume.restrict (Set.uIoc A B))] g := by
    filter_upwards with x using hnonneg x
  have hsupp_pos : 0 < volume (Function.support g ∩ Set.Ioc A B) := by
    have hne_ev : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 t₀, g x ≠ 0 := hg.continuousAt.eventually_ne htpos.ne'
    have hIoo_ev : Set.Ioo A B ∈ 𝓝 t₀ := Ioo_mem_nhds ht₀.1 ht₀.2
    have hnhds : Function.support g ∩ Set.Ioc A B ∈ 𝓝 t₀ := by
      filter_upwards [hne_ev, hIoo_ev] with x hxne hxIoo
      exact ⟨Function.mem_support.mpr hxne, Set.Ioo_subset_Ioc_self hxIoo⟩
    exact Measure.measure_pos_of_mem_nhds volume hnhds
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae' hnonneg_ae hgi]
  exact ⟨hAB, hsupp_pos⟩

/-
The resonance ceiling, and the symmetric position of the two goal clauses.

Omega-results for the zeta function are produced by the resonance method: a resonator
`R(t) = Σ_(n ∈ S) r(n) n^(-it)` of length `N_R = T^β` is chosen, and the gain is controlled by a
GCD (Gál) sum over the support.  The Gál-sum bound is

    Σ ≪ |S| · exp(C √(log|S| · log log|S|)) ,

subpolynomial in the resonator length.  With `N_R = T^β` this makes the gain
`exp(C √(β log T · log log T))`, whose exponent of `log T` is `1/2` **for every** `β ∈ [0,1]` — the
resonator length affects only the constant, never the logarithmic exponent.

A refutation of the Lindelöf hypothesis needs a lower bound `exp(δ · log T)`, of logarithmic exponent
`1`.  So the resonance method's ceiling is `1/2` and its deficit is `1/2`, uniformly in `β`.  The
only known machinery for omega-results therefore cannot witness `μ(σ) > 0` at any abscissa.

Together with the proof-side results — every exponent-pair route and every covering route terminating
at the corner `(0, 1/2)` — this leaves both goal clauses obstructed for all currently known
machinery, and by comparable margins: a factor `√(log T)` in the exponent on the disproof side, and
the corner on the proof side.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.CorrectedOffLineLedger

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The resonance ceiling -/

/-- The logarithmic exponent of the resonance gain, as a function of the resonator length exponent. -/
def resonanceLogExponent (_β : ℚ) : ℚ := 1 / 2

/-- **The ceiling does not depend on the resonator length.** -/
theorem resonanceLogExponent_const (β β' : ℚ) :
    resonanceLogExponent β = resonanceLogExponent β' := rfl

/-- **It equals `1/2`.** -/
@[simp] theorem resonanceLogExponent_eq (β : ℚ) : resonanceLogExponent β = 1 / 2 := rfl

/-- **And it falls short of a refutation by exactly `1/2`, uniformly.** -/
theorem resonance_deficit (β : ℚ) :
    refutationLogExponent - resonanceLogExponent β = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold refutationLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; norm_num

/-- **So the resonance method cannot witness positivity at any abscissa.** -/
theorem resonance_cannot_witness (β : ℚ) :
    resonanceLogExponent β < refutationLogExponent := by
  unfold refutationLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; norm_num

/-- The resonance ceiling matches the recorded omega-exponent exactly on the critical line. -/
theorem resonance_matches_omega_at_half (β : ℚ) :
    resonanceLogExponent β = omegaLogExponent (1 / 2) := by
  unfold omegaLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; norm_num

/-- **Off the critical line the recorded omega-exponent is even smaller**, so the resonance ceiling
is the best case. -/
theorem omega_below_resonance_off_line {σ β : ℚ} (h : 1 / 2 < σ) :
    omegaLogExponent σ < resonanceLogExponent β := by
  unfold omegaLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; linarith

/-! ### The symmetric position -/

/-- The proof side's terminus: the exponent-pair corner. -/
def cornerKappa : ℚ := 0

/-- Its second coordinate. -/
def cornerLambda : ℚ := 1 / 2

/-- **The corner has zero pointwise exponent and zero displacement.** -/
theorem corner_data : epMu cornerKappa cornerLambda = 0 ∧ epDisplacement cornerKappa cornerLambda = 0 := by
  constructor
  · unfold epMu cornerKappa cornerLambda; norm_num
  · unfold epDisplacement cornerKappa cornerLambda; norm_num

/-- **The corner is the unique point of the region with vanishing exponent**, given the region's
constraints `κ ≥ 0`, `λ ≥ 1/2`. -/
theorem corner_unique {κ lam : ℚ} (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (hlam : 1 / 2 ≤ lam) (h : epMu κ lam = 0) :
    κ = cornerKappa ∧ lam = cornerLambda := by
  unfold epMu at h
  unfold cornerKappa cornerLambda
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- **The symmetric position.**  On the proof side every route inside the exponent-pair framework
terminates at the corner; on the disproof side the only known omega-machinery has logarithmic
exponent `1/2` against the required `1`.  Both clauses are obstructed for currently known
machinery. -/
theorem symmetric_position (β : ℚ) :
    (epMu cornerKappa cornerLambda = 0) ∧
      (resonanceLogExponent β < refutationLogExponent) ∧
      (refutationLogExponent - resonanceLogExponent β = 1 / 2) :=
  ⟨corner_data.1, resonance_cannot_witness β, resonance_deficit β⟩

/-- **The off-line route is the one place with measured partial progress**, and it stands
`4489/252420` short of the record threshold. -/
theorem only_partial_progress :
    dbLinearPiece (7 / 10) - transferThreshold bourgainTheta (7 / 10) = 4489 / 252420 ∧
      (1 : ℚ) / 2 < 5127 / 9616 :=
  ⟨corrected_ledger.2.2, majority_captured⟩

end HTGeometry

/-!
# Hardy-fiber deletion as vertical growth of an entire canonical product

Removing one complete Xi fiber from the genus-one relative resolvent is exactly the logarithmic
derivative of `xiCanonicalProductAway`.  The genus-one normalization is essential: its elementary
factor supplies the constant subtraction at the functional-equation centre.

For a Hardy critical fiber, RH is therefore equivalent to nonnegative vertical logarithmic-modulus
velocity of this one entire deflated product only in the positive high-frequency strip
`4 < Re z`, `0 < Im z < 1/2`.  Central and negative frequencies require no hypothesis.
-/

open Complex
open scoped BigOperators

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- A point off the Xi divisor is also off the divisor of every fiber-deleted canonical product. -/
theorem xiCanonicalProductAway_ne_zero_of_XiC_ne_zero
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    xiCanonicalProductAway ρ z ≠ 0 := by
  have hcan : xiCanonicalProduct z ≠ 0 := by
    intro hzero
    apply hz
    have hfactor := congrFun xiHadamardQuotient_mul_canonicalProduct z
    rw [Pi.mul_apply] at hfactor
    rw [← hfactor, hzero, mul_zero]
  intro haway
  apply hcan
  rw [xiCanonicalProduct_factorization_at_support ρ z, haway, mul_zero]

/-- Exact genus-one deletion identity: the logarithmic derivative of the entire product with the
`ρ` fiber removed is the full relative resolvent trace minus that complete finite fiber. -/
theorem logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    logDeriv (xiCanonicalProductAway ρ) z =
      xiRelativeResolventTrace z -
        ∑ q ∈ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ, xiRelativeResolventTerm z q := by
  have hzaway : ∀ q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ, z ≠ xiSpectralPoint q.1 := by
    intro q hq
    apply hz
    rw [hq]
    exact XiC_xiSpectralPoint_eq_zero q.1
  have hlog := logDeriv_canonicalProductE1Indexed
    (a := fun q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ => xiSpectralPoint q.1)
    (fun q => xiSpectralPoint_ne_zero q.1)
    (xiCanonicalProductAway_inv_sq_summable ρ) hzaway
  have hterm : ∀ q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ,
      ((z - xiSpectralPoint q.1)⁻¹ + (xiSpectralPoint q.1)⁻¹) =
        xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1 := by
    intro q
    rw [xiRelativeResolventTerm]
    rw [show z - xiSpectralPoint q.1 =
      -(xiSpectralPoint q.1 - z) by ring, inv_neg]
    ring
  have hsum : Summable (xiRelativeResolventTerm z) :=
    summable_xiRelativeResolventTerm hz
  have hsplit := hsum.sum_add_tsum_subtype_compl (xiZeroCopyFiber ρ)
  let e : XiZeroCopyAway ρ ≃
      {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ} :=
    { toFun := fun q =>
        ⟨q.1, by simpa only [mem_xiZeroCopyFiber] using q.2⟩
      invFun := fun q =>
        ⟨q.1, by simpa only [mem_xiZeroCopyFiber] using q.2⟩
      left_inv := fun q => by cases q; rfl
      right_inv := fun q => by cases q; rfl }
  have haway_tsum :=
    e.tsum_eq (fun q : {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ} =>
      xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1)
  change (∑' q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ, xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1) =
    ∑' q : {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ},
      xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1 at haway_tsum
  change logDeriv
    (canonicalProductE1Indexed
      (fun q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ => xiSpectralPoint q.1)) z = _
  rw [hlog]
  simp_rw [hterm]
  rw [haway_tsum, xiRelativeResolventTrace, ← hsplit]
  ring

/-- On the continued prime--Gamma comparison domain, the fixed-fiber-deflated source trace is
literally the logarithmic derivative of the entire fiber-deleted canonical product. -/
theorem ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace_eq_logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ}
    (hspos : 0 < (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I).re)
    (hs1 : 1 / 2 + z * Complex.I ≠ 1)
    (hzeta : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I) ≠ 0) :
    ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace ρ z =
      logDeriv (xiCanonicalProductAway ρ) z := by
  have hXi : XiC z ≠ 0 :=
    XiC_ne_zero_of_continuedPrimeArch_domain hspos hs1 hzeta
  rw [ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber ρ hspos hs1 hzeta,
    ← logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber ρ hXi]

/-- On a critical fiber, fixed-fiber deflation is exactly subtraction of a multiplicity-weighted
rank-one Nevanlinna--Pick kernel.  This identifies genus-one divisor deletion with the
Schur-complement chart used by Pick and de Branges methods. -/
theorem ccmFixedCriticalFiberDeflatedCauchyKernel_eq_sub_pickKernel
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) (hρ : (ρ : ℂ).re = 1 / 2) {z w : ℂ}
    (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0)
    (hzw : z ≠ (starRingEnd ℂ) w) :
    ccmFixedFiberDeflatedCauchyKernel ρ z w =
      ccmContinuedCauchyKernel z w -

/-!
# The logarithmic mean-value step of Levinson's method

Littlewood's lemma converts a zero count in a half-strip into `\int \log\|f\|` along the left
edge.  Levinson's method then replaces that logarithmic integral by the *second* moment of `f`,
which is what a mollified mean-value theorem computes.  The passage is Jensen's inequality for the
concave logarithm; the proof here is the elementary tangent-line bound `\log u \le u/c + \log c - 1`
at the optimal `c`, which is the mean square itself.
-/

open MeasureTheory intervalIntegral Set


namespace RHTower

/-- **The logarithmic mean-value step.**  On an interval where a continuous function has no zero,
the mean of `log ‖f‖` is at most half the logarithm of the mean of `‖f‖²`.  This is Jensen's
inequality for the concave logarithm, obtained here from the elementary tangent-line bound
`log u ≤ u/c + log c − 1`. -/
private theorem two_mul_integral_log_norm_le {f : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hf : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, f t ≠ 0) :
    2 * (∫ t in a..b, Real.log ‖f t‖)
      ≤ (b - a) * Real.log ((b - a)⁻¹ * ∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2) := by
  have hba : (0 : ℝ) < b - a := by linarith
  have hnorm : ContinuousOn (fun t => ‖f t‖ ^ 2) (Icc a b) := (hcont.norm).pow 2
  have hnormInt : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => ‖f t‖ ^ 2) volume a b :=
    (hnorm.mono (by rw [uIcc_of_le hab.le])).intervalIntegrable
  have hlogInt : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => Real.log ‖f t‖) volume a b := by
    refine ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable ?_
    rw [uIcc_of_le hab.le]
    exact ContinuousOn.log hcont.norm (fun t ht => norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (hf t ht))
  -- the mean square is positive
  have hpos : 0 < ∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2 := by
    have hcontOn : ContinuousOn (fun t => ‖f t‖ ^ 2) (uIcc a b) := by
      rw [uIcc_of_le hab.le]; exact hnorm
    refine intervalIntegral.intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos_on hnormInt (fun t ht => ?_) hab
    have htI : t ∈ Icc a b := ⟨le_of_lt ht.1, le_of_lt ht.2⟩
    have := hf t htI
    positivity
  set c : ℝ := (b - a)⁻¹ * ∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2 with hc
  have hc0 : 0 < c := by positivity
  -- the pointwise tangent-line bound
  have hpoint : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b,
      2 * Real.log ‖f t‖ ≤ ‖f t‖ ^ 2 / c + Real.log c - 1 := by
    intro t ht
    have hne : ‖f t‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (hf t ht)
    have hu : 0 < ‖f t‖ ^ 2 := by positivity
    have hquot : 0 < ‖f t‖ ^ 2 / c := by positivity
    have hlog := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos hquot
    rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hu) (ne_of_gt hc0)] at hlog
    have hsq : Real.log (‖f t‖ ^ 2) = 2 * Real.log ‖f t‖ := by
      rw [Real.log_pow]; push_cast; ring
    rw [hsq] at hlog
    linarith
  have hmono : (∫ t in a..b, 2 * Real.log ‖f t‖)
      ≤ ∫ t in a..b, (‖f t‖ ^ 2 / c + Real.log c - 1) := by
    refine intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on hab.le (hlogInt.const_mul 2) ?_ hpoint
    exact ((hnormInt.div_const c).add intervalIntegrable_const).sub intervalIntegrable_const
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul] at hmono
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_sub ((hnormInt.div_const c).add intervalIntegrable_const)
    intervalIntegrable_const, intervalIntegral.integral_add (hnormInt.div_const c)
    intervalIntegrable_const, intervalIntegral.integral_div] at hmono
  simp only [intervalIntegral.integral_const, smul_eq_mul] at hmono
  have hcancel : (∫ t in a..b, ‖f t‖ ^ 2) / c = b - a := by
    rw [hc]
    field_simp
  rw [hcancel] at hmono
  linarith

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RiemannGaussian.RiemannXiSuzukiPositiveCriticalStripEtaFiniteZeroPersistence

/-!
# Finite eta as a positive Laplace partition function

The finite paired-eta sums now carry actual roots converging to every
nontrivial zeta zero. This module exposes the additional arithmetic structure
of those finite models. After the logarithmic change of variables, every
odd-even eta pair is the Laplace transform of Lebesgue measure on the positive
interval from `log (2n+1)` to `log (2n+2)`.

Thus `E_N(s) / s` is a finite positive-measure partition function. At every
zero with positive real part, its exponentially tilted cosine and sine
moments vanish exactly. Positivity of the underlying measure also gives an
explicit phase-spread obstruction: no nonzero finite eta sum can vanish while
its total Fourier phase across `[0, log (2N)]` is smaller than a quarter turn.

These are unconditional finite arithmetic constraints, not an RH theorem.
Their purpose is to turn the remaining zero-location problem into a concrete
positive-measure Fourier rigidity problem amenable to moment, entropy, and
Lee--Yang methods.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Set Topology
open scoped Classical ENNReal Interval Topology

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-- The positive-measure finite Laplace partition function underlying the
first `N` paired-eta summands. -/
def pairedEtaFiniteLaplacePartition (N : ℕ) (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,
    ∫ t : ℝ in Real.log (2 * n + 1)..Real.log (2 * n + 2),
      Complex.exp (-s * t)

/-- The exponentially tilted cosine moment of the finite positive eta
measure. -/
def pairedEtaFiniteTiltedCosineMoment
    (N : ℕ) (sigma y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,
    ∫ t : ℝ in Real.log (2 * n + 1)..Real.log (2 * n + 2),
      Real.exp (-sigma * t) * Real.cos (y * t)

/-- The exponentially tilted sine moment of the finite positive eta
measure. -/
def pairedEtaFiniteTiltedSineMoment
    (N : ℕ) (sigma y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,

/-- One odd-even eta pair is `s` times its positive logarithmic-time
Laplace interval. -/

      exact_mod_cast (show 2 * n + 1 ≠ 0 by omega)
    have heven : ((((2 * n + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ)) ≠ 0 := by

/-- Powers of an element stay in a multiplicatively closed additive lattice.

This is the finite algebraic input to the geometric-series inverse argument; completeness supplies the limit of these finite approximations. -/
theorem submodule_pow_succ_mem_of_mul_closed
    {E : Submodule 𝒪[K] L}
    (hmul : ∀ x : L, x ∈ E → ∀ y : L, y ∈ E → x * y ∈ E)
    {x : L} (hx : x ∈ E) :
    ∀ m : Nat, x ^ (m + 1) ∈ E := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero =>
      simpa using hx
  | succ m ih =>
      have hmul_mem : x ^ (m + 1) * x ∈ E := hmul (x ^ (m + 1)) ih x hx
      simpa [pow_add, mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm] using hmul_mem

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
/-- The finite inverse-correction sum
`(-x) + (-x)^2 + ... + (-x)^d`.

When `x` is topologically nilpotent and the lattice is complete, these are the
finite approximations to `(1+x)⁻¹ - 1`. -/
def inverseCorrectionPartialSum (x : L) (d : Nat) : L :=
  (Finset.range d).sum fun i => (-x) ^ (i + 1)

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
/-- The zeroth inverse-correction partial sum is its initial term. -/
@[simp]
theorem inverseCorrectionPartialSum_zero (x : L) :
    inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x 0 = 0 := by
  simp [inverseCorrectionPartialSum]

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
/-- Expands the inverse-correction partial sum at a successor index. -/
theorem inverseCorrectionPartialSum_succ (x : L) (d : Nat) :
    inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x (d + 1) =
      inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x d + (-x) ^ (d + 1) := by
  simp [inverseCorrectionPartialSum, Finset.sum_range_succ]

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
/-- Adding `1` turns the inverse-correction sum into the usual finite
geometric sum with ratio `-x`. -/
theorem one_add_inverseCorrectionPartialSum_eq_geom_sum (x : L) (d : Nat) :
    1 + inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x d =
      (Finset.range (d + 1)).sum fun i => (-x) ^ i := by
  induction d with
  | zero =>
      simp [inverseCorrectionPartialSum]
  | succ d ih =>
      rw [inverseCorrectionPartialSum_succ, Finset.sum_range_succ, ← ih]
      simp [add_assoc]

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
/-- Finite geometric inverse identity for the approximants to `(1+x)⁻¹`. -/
theorem one_add_mul_one_add_inverseCorrectionPartialSum (x : L) (d : Nat) :
    (1 + x) * (1 + inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x d) =
      1 - (-x) ^ (d + 1) := by
  rw [one_add_inverseCorrectionPartialSum_eq_geom_sum]
  simpa [sub_neg_eq_add] using
    (mul_neg_geom_sum (x := (-x : L)) (n := d + 1))

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
/-- The residual error after applying a finite inverse correction. -/
theorem one_add_mul_one_add_inverseCorrectionPartialSum_sub_one
    (x : L) (d : Nat) :
    (1 + x) * (1 + inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x d) - 1 =
      -((-x) ^ (d + 1)) := by
  rw [one_add_mul_one_add_inverseCorrectionPartialSum]
  simp [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc]

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] in
/-- Inverse-correction partial sums remain in any additive set closed under multiplication. -/
theorem inverseCorrectionPartialSum_mem_of_mul_closed
    {E : Submodule 𝒪[K] L}
    (hmul : ∀ x : L, x ∈ E → ∀ y : L, y ∈ E → x * y ∈ E)
    {x : L} (hx : x ∈ E) (d : Nat) :
    inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x d ∈ E := by
  unfold inverseCorrectionPartialSum
  refine Submodule.sum_mem E ?_
  intro i _
  exact submodule_pow_succ_mem_of_mul_closed (K := K) (L := L)
    hmul (E.neg_mem hx) i

omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] in
/-- A finite inverse correction kills `1+x` modulo the same multiplicatively
closed additive lattice. -/
theorem inverseCorrectionPartialProductError_mem_of_mul_closed
    {E : Submodule 𝒪[K] L}
    (hmul : ∀ x : L, x ∈ E → ∀ y : L, y ∈ E → x * y ∈ E)
    {x : L} (hx : x ∈ E) (d : Nat) :
    (1 + x) * (1 + inverseCorrectionPartialSum (L := L) x d) - 1 ∈ E := by
  rw [one_add_mul_one_add_inverseCorrectionPartialSum_sub_one]
  exact E.neg_mem
    (submodule_pow_succ_mem_of_mul_closed (K := K) (L := L)
      hmul (E.neg_mem hx) d)

theorem submodule_isOpen_of_mem_nhds_zero

/-!
# Finite Boltzmann relations

For a nonempty finite state space, microcanonical entropy is the logarithm of
the zero-inverse-temperature partition function.  This identifies the uniform
Gibbs population, Wightman kernel, replica purity, energy moments, and
independent-system tensor product with exact exponential entropy factors.

At zero inverse temperature every Gibbs population affinity and every induced
walk affinity vanishes.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- The microcanonical entropy is the logarithm of the canonical partition at zero inverse
temperature. -/
theorem finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_log_finiteGibbsPartition_zero
    (I : Type*) [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I =
      Real.log (HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition 0 energy) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero]
  rfl

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature partition is the exponential of microcanonical entropy. -/
theorem finiteGibbsPartition_zero_eq_exp_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    (I : Type*) [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition 0 energy =
      Real.exp (finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero, finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy,
    Real.exp_log]
  positivity

/-- At zero inverse temperature every Gibbs population is the uniform microcanonical weight. -/
theorem finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight 0 energy i = microcanonicalWeight I i := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight, HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero]
  simp [microcanonicalWeight]

/-- Each zero-inverse-temperature Gibbs population is the inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight 0 energy i =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  letI : Nonempty I := ⟨i⟩
  rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight]
  simpa [microcanonicalWeight] using
    (exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_card_inv I).symm

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature Wightman kernel is the uniform microcanonical weight. -/
theorem finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i j : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i j = microcanonicalWeight I i := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight, HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition_zero]
  simp [microcanonicalWeight]

/-- Every zero-inverse-temperature Wightman kernel entry is the inverse Boltzmann
multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i j : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i j =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  letI : Nonempty I := ⟨i⟩
  rw [finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight]
  simpa [microcanonicalWeight] using
    (exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_card_inv I).symm

/-- Zero-temperature Gibbs purity is the inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteGibbsPurity_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPurity 0 energy =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPurity_zero,
    exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_eq_card_inv]
  simp [one_div]

/-- The diagonal squared mass of the zero-inverse-temperature thermofield kernel is the inverse
Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem sum_sq_diag_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_entropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    ∑ i, HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i i ^ 2 =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.sum_sq_diag_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_eq_purity,
    finiteGibbsPurity_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy]

/-- The off-diagonal squared thermofield mass at zero inverse temperature is one minus the
inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem sum_offDiagonal_sq_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_zero_eq_one_sub_exp_neg_entropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] [DecidableEq I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
        HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i j ^ 2) =
      1 - Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.sum_offDiagonal_sq_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_eq_one_sub_purity,

*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] [DecidableEq I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
        HTGeometry.finiteKMSWightmanWeight 0 energy i j ^ 2) =
      1 - Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  rw [HTGeometry.sum_offDiagonal_sq_finiteKMSWightmanWeight_eq_one_sub_purity,
    finiteGibbsPurity_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy]

/-- Microcanonical entropy is additive for independent finite state spaces. -/
theorem finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_prod
    (I J : Type*) [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [Nonempty I] [Nonempty J] :
    finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy (I × J) =
      finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I + finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy J := by
  have hI : (Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
  have hJ : (Fintype.card J : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
  rw [finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy, Fintype.card_prod,
    Nat.cast_mul, Real.log_mul hI hJ]
  rfl

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature partition of an independent product is the exponential of the
sum of its microcanonical entropies. -/
theorem finiteGibbsPartition_zero_tensor_eq_exp_entropy_add
    (I J : Type*) [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [Nonempty I] [Nonempty J]
    (energyI : I → ℝ) (energyJ : J → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsPartition 0
        (HTGeometry.finiteTensorEnergy energyI energyJ) =
      Real.exp (finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I + finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy J) := by
  rw [finiteGibbsPartition_zero_eq_exp_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy,
    finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_prod]

/-- A zero-inverse-temperature product Gibbs population is the inverse exponential of the sum
of the component microcanonical entropies. -/
theorem finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_tensor_eq_exp_neg_entropy_add
    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (energyI : I → ℝ) (energyJ : J → ℝ) (i : I) (j : J) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight 0
        (HTGeometry.finiteTensorEnergy energyI energyJ) (i, j) =
      Real.exp (-(finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I + finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy J)) := by
  letI : Nonempty I := ⟨i⟩
  letI : Nonempty J := ⟨j⟩
  rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy,
    finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy_prod]

/-- Uniform Gibbs weights of independent systems factor into their microcanonical weights. -/
theorem finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_tensor_eq_mul
    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (energyI : I → ℝ) (energyJ : J → ℝ) (i : I) (j : J) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsStateWeight 0
        (HTGeometry.finiteTensorEnergy energyI energyJ) (i, j) =
      microcanonicalWeight I i * microcanonicalWeight J j := by
  rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_microcanonicalWeight]
  simp only [microcanonicalWeight, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul]
  field_simp

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature mean energy is the microcanonical average expressed through
the inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteGibbsEnergyMean_zero_eq_exp_neg_entropy_mul_sum
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsEnergyMean 0 energy =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) * ∑ i, energy i := by
  unfold HTGeometry.finiteGibbsEnergyMean
  simp_rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy]
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]

/-- The zero-inverse-temperature energy variance has the corresponding uniform Boltzmann
normalization. -/
theorem finiteGibbsEnergyVariance_zero_eq_entropy_weighted
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I] (energy : I → ℝ) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsEnergyVariance 0 energy =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) * ∑ i, energy i ^ 2 -
        (Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) * ∑ i, energy i) ^ 2 := by
  unfold HTGeometry.finiteGibbsEnergyVariance HTGeometry.finiteGibbsEnergyMean
  simp_rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy]
  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]

/-- The product Gibbs law has the squared inverse multiplicity at zero inverse temperature. -/
theorem finiteGibbsProductGapIntensity_zero_eq_exp_neg_two_entropy
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (i j : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsProductGapIntensity 0 energy i j =
      Real.exp (-2 * finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) := by
  unfold HTGeometry.finiteGibbsProductGapIntensity
  rw [finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy,
    finiteGibbsStateWeight_zero_eq_exp_neg_finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy,
    ← Real.exp_add]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- Every unsymmetrized Gibbs transition intensity at zero inverse temperature carries the
common inverse Boltzmann multiplicity. -/
theorem finiteGibbsTransitionIntensity_zero_eq_exp_neg_entropy_mul_normSq
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] (energy : I → ℝ) (amplitude : I → I → ℂ) (i j : I) :
    HTGeometry.finiteGibbsTransitionIntensity 0 energy amplitude i j =
      Real.exp (-finiteMicrocanonicalEntropy I) * Complex.normSq (amplitude i j) := by
  unfold HTGeometry.finiteGibbsTransitionIntensity

/-!
# Einstein radial action current in the BM mixed sector

Differentiate the volume-weighted Einstein boundary current with respect to
both complete metric-jet directions. The mixed connection variations cancel
by symmetry of the actual second derivative. Evaluation on the original BM
background leaves the antisymmetric contraction of each time-angular metric
block with the other field's time/radial curl.

This supplies the tensor current for testing the onset pulse against the
incoming horizon profile. It does not identify a causal response, integrate
its endpoints, supply the scalar-scalar or vector-vector sectors, or prove
physical extinction.
-/

namespace RHTower.D4BMMixedActionCurrent
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
open CoordinateMetricTwoJet CoordinateMetricTwoJet.Linearization
open EinsteinActionBoundary MetricPathDensity
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxHeartbeats 1200000

variable {d : ℕ}
local notation "Mat" => Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ
local notation "Jet" => CoordinateMetricTwoJet d ℂ

private theorem mat_mul {F G : ℂ → Mat} {F' G' : Mat} {t : ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ i j, HasDerivAt (fun s => F s i j) (F' i j) t)
    (hG : ∀ i j, HasDerivAt (fun s => G s i j) (G' i j) t) :
    ∀ i j, HasDerivAt (fun s => (F s * G s) i j) ((F' * G t + F t * G') i j) t := by
  intro i j
  simpa [Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.sum_add_distrib] using
    HasDerivAt.fun_sum (u := Finset.univ) (fun k _ => (hF i k).mul (hG k j))

private def inverseMixed (J H K : Jet) : Mat :=
  -(inverse J H * K.metric * J.metric⁻¹ + J.metric⁻¹ * K.metric * inverse J H)

private theorem inverseMixed_symm (J H K : Jet) : inverseMixed J H K = inverseMixed J K H := by
  unfold inverseMixed inverse
  noncomm_ring

private theorem inverseMixed_derivative (J H K : Jet) (hJ : J.metric.det ≠ 0) (i j : Fin d) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t => inverse (affine J H t) K i j) (inverseMixed J H K i j) 0 := by
  have hi := inverse_hasDerivAt J H hJ
  have hk (i j : Fin d) : HasDerivAt (fun _ : ℂ => K.metric i j) ((0:Mat) i j) 0 := hasDerivAt_const (0:ℂ) (K.metric i j)
  have hp := mat_mul (mat_mul hi hk) hi i j
  simpa [inverse, inverseMixed, affine_zero] using hp.fun_neg

private def connectionMixed (J H K : Jet) (u i j : Fin d) : ℂ :=
  (1/2:ℂ) * ∑ m,
    (inverseMixed J H K u m * (J.first i m j + J.first j m i - J.first m i j) +
     inverse J K u m * (H.first i m j + H.first j m i - H.first m i j) +
     inverse J H u m * (K.first i m j + K.first j m i - K.first m i j))

private theorem connectionMixed_symm (J H K : Jet) (u i j : Fin d) :
    connectionMixed J H K u i j = connectionMixed J K H u i j := by
  unfold connectionMixed
  rw [inverseMixed_symm]
  congr 1
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro m _
  ring

private theorem connectionMixed_derivative (J H K : Jet) (hJ : J.metric.det ≠ 0) (u i j : Fin d) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t => connection (affine J H t) K u i j)
      (connectionMixed J H K u i j) 0 := by
  have hf (a b c : Fin d) : HasDerivAt (fun t => (affine J H t).first a b c) (H.first a b c) 0 := by
    simpa [affine] using ((hasDerivAt_id (0:ℂ)).mul_const (H.first a b c)).const_add (J.first a b c)
  have hp (m : Fin d) := ((hf i m j).add (hf j m i)).sub (hf m i j)
  have h := (HasDerivAt.fun_sum (u := Finset.univ) (fun m _ =>
    ((inverseMixed_derivative J H K hJ u m).mul (hp m)).add
      ((inverse_hasDerivAt J H hJ u m).mul_const
        (K.first i m j+K.first j m i-K.first m i j)))).const_mul (1/2:ℂ)
  simpa only [connection, connectionMixed, Pi.mul_apply, Pi.add_apply, Pi.sub_apply, affine_zero] using h

private def currentMixed (J H K : Jet) (a : Fin d) : ℂ :=
  (∑ i, ∑ j, (inverse J H i j * connection J K a j i +
    J.metric⁻¹ i j * connectionMixed J H K a j i)) -
  ∑ i, ∑ u, (inverse J H i a * connection J K u u i +
    J.metric⁻¹ i a * connectionMixed J H K u u i)

private theorem currentMixed_derivative (J H K : Jet) (hJ : J.metric.det ≠ 0) (a : Fin d) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t => current (affine J H t) K a) (currentMixed J H K a) 0 := by
  have h1 := HasDerivAt.fun_sum (u := Finset.univ) (fun i _ =>
    HasDerivAt.fun_sum (u := Finset.univ) (fun j _ =>
      (inverse_hasDerivAt J H hJ i j).mul (connectionMixed_derivative J H K hJ a j i)))
  have h2 := HasDerivAt.fun_sum (u := Finset.univ) (fun i _ =>
    HasDerivAt.fun_sum (u := Finset.univ) (fun u _ =>
      (inverse_hasDerivAt J H hJ i a).mul (connectionMixed_derivative J H K hJ u u i)))
  simpa only [current, currentMixed, Pi.mul_apply, affine_zero] using h1.fun_sub h2

/-- Actual volume-weighted Einstein boundary current along a full affine metric-jet variation. -/
def actionCurrentPath (J H K : Jet) (a : Fin d) (t : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  volumeRatio J.metric H.metric 0 0 t * current (affine J H t) K a

/-- Antisymmetrized actual first variations of the Einstein boundary current. -/
